reading: On the 9.84M comparison decoder at four threads, the widest instance and every thread are the measured winners nearly everywhere. Under bf16 none of the 93 alternatives reads faster at its sites: 88 read slower, each interval wholly above 1.0, and 5 resolve neither way (the embedding's three worker counts x1.027-x1.066, the o projection at three workers x1.078, the embedding gradient's scatter at one x0.922 within 0.824-1.031). The AVX-512 instance in place of AMX costs the GEMMs x4.74 (the head's VJP) to x10.11 (the gate/up VJP) and the attention x1.34 forward and x2.34 backward; the portable instance costs the GEMMs x274-x646 and the attention x54 and x108; one, two and three workers cost x0.92-x3.82, x1.03-x1.99 and x1.07-x1.36. So choose_dispatch keeps the default dispatch, and its arm is a third trainer running the default program: x0.9875 (95% interval 0.9625-1.0132) against the first, beside the A/A control's x1.0012 (0.9756-1.0275). Under binary32 one alternative reads faster: the embedding gradient's scatter -- run on the pool in the serial order -- at one worker, x0.848 (0.734-0.980) of its four-thread default at its sites; 89 read slower and 3 resolve neither way (the embedding's three worker counts). AVX2 in place of AVX-512 costs the GEMMs x1.37-x1.90 and the attention x2.75 and x2.60, the portable instance x71-x81 and x31 and x47. choose_dispatch takes the scatter at one worker, its readings predicting x0.9998 for the step (the scatter is a small part of it), and end to end the chosen dispatch reads x1.0101 (0.9901-1.0304) beside the A/A control's x0.9892 (0.9727-1.0060): not resolvable on this host. The dispatches the measurement prices slowest (every GEMM and attention kind on the portable instance, the other kernels at their slowest worker counts) and on the portable instance run x216.5 (183.9-254.9) and x215.1 (182.8-253.0) of the default under bf16 -- 18.8 s a step against 79.5 ms -- where the readings predicted x240.7 and x239.8, and x63.2 (59.7-66.9) and x62.5 (59.5-65.7) under binary32 -- 14.0 s against 216.7 ms -- where they predicted x64.9 and x64.5: the sites' prices hold over the whole step, and they are the vector units' price. Every trainer of a rotation leaves one state, bit for bit (893 records a four-step program under every dispatch). The table, its raw readings round by round and the end-to-end milliseconds are in each record. Carried into K_BCIR's candidates (carry.py, PX-3b-2): the binary32 table's one pick -- the scatter at one worker -- becomes one measured entry (train.scatter, 393,216, t1, Q8 217); the four-step pack's plan runs its 4 scatter claims at gather@t1 among 893, the C lowers it to exactly the program the chosen dispatch states, and the lowered pack trains that program's state bit for bit. The bf16 table has no pick, so no entry: the plan is the default's, its lowering the default program.
